title: Google DeepMind Research Scientist Job 2026: Apply for AI for Science and Medicine Research in Mountain View, California
summary: Are you a researcher passionate about artificial intelligence, biomedical research, computational biology, cancer research, or using machine learning to solve some of the world s most complex scientific and medical challenges? About the Google DeepMind AI for Science and Medicine Opportunity Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to tackle complex problems in science and healthcare. Rather than limiting AI to conventional applications such as search, recommendation systems, or language generation, researchers are developing increasingly sophisticated models capable of helping scientists understand biological systems, discover molecules, predict disease processes, analyze medical information, and accelerate scientific experimentation. Google DeepMind has positioned scientific discovery as an important area of its work. Its careers information highlights examples of AI being used to help scientists understand molecular interactions, advance research into diseases, discover candidate materials, and improve scientific forecasting. The Research Scientist opportunity described here is aimed at researchers interested in pushing this type of work further. AI can potentially contribute by helping researchers analyze complex biological data, identify patterns that are difficult to detect manually, model biological processes, generate scientific hypotheses, and accelerate the development of new approaches. For a researcher, therefore, the attraction of this opportunity is not simply working for a globally recognized technology organization. It is the possibility of applying advanced computational methods to questions with significant scientific and medical consequences. Google DeepMind s careers information emphasizes its goal of developing breakthrough AI while using the technology to advance science and potentially improve lives globally. Automating aspects of scientific experimentation. Analyzing high-dimensional scientific data. Improving computational approaches to scientific discovery. The field brings together machine learning, mathematics, statistics, computing, and domain-specific scientific knowledge. 2. AI for Medicine AI for Medicine focuses on using artificial intelligence to address medical and healthcare problems. Researchers interested in this opportunity should be able to explain clearly how their work could contribute to AI-driven scientific or medical discovery. 3. Multi-modal biomedical data. Computational approaches to cancer research. 4. Computational Biology Computational biology combines computational methods with biological research. title: EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027: UK Research Organisations Can Apply for Up to £62,500 to Host Policy Fellowships
summary: Applications are now open for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027 , an initiative providing UK research organisations with funding of up to £62,500 to establish and deliver Policy Fellowship programmes for public and civil servants. The programme is designed to strengthen connections between the UK research community and the public sector by creating opportunities for public and civil servants to spend dedicated time engaging with academics and researchers on real-world policy challenges. Eligible research organisations across the United Kingdom can apply to EvEx to develop and run their own funded Policy Fellowship programme. Successful organisations will host Policy Fellows between January and May 2027 , providing opportunities for problem-solving, professional development, network building, knowledge exchange and access to academic expertise. Approximately 10 EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are expected to be offered across the UK during the 2026–2027 programme cycle, with applications closing at midday on 8 October 2026 . About the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Programme The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship programme has been created to increase the number, capacity and diversity of Policy Fellowship opportunities available across the United Kingdom. Through the programme, research organisations can receive financial and practical support to establish and deliver fellowships that connect researchers with UK public and civil servants. Research organisations selected as hosts will be responsible for developing programmes that allow participating public and civil servants to spend meaningful time engaging with researchers and exploring specific policy questions and challenges. Policy Fellows can be selected from any public bodies and across all levels of seniority . The programme is intended to provide participating public and civil servants with opportunities to: Explore specific policy challenges and questions with relevant researchers. Access specialist academic and research expertise. Develop new approaches to problem-solving. Build relationships between researchers and policymakers. Expand professional networks. Participate in professional development and knowledge-exchange activities. Explore policy issues through interdisciplinary academic perspectives. The Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are specifically intended to create additional capacity and diversity by supporting research organisations outside the existing EvEx consortium to establish their own Policy Fellowship programmes. This funding call is complementary to EvEx s separate call for individual and small-team Policy Fellows, which is administered and hosted directly by the EvEx consortium. Funding Available Through the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Eligible organisations may apply for a maximum budget of £62,500 to deliver their proposed Associate Policy Fellowship programme. EvEx suggests that organisations use the funding to offer approximately three to 10 Associate Policy Fellowships . However, the programme also allows some flexibility in how organisations design their fellowship activities. EvEx is open to proposals that use alternative approaches to engaging Associate Policy Fellows, provided that participating public or civil servants spend a minimum of five days during the five-month programme period exploring policy questions with research input from one or more participating research organisations. This flexibility gives organisations the opportunity to develop a fellowship model suited to their institutional strengths, available expertise and the policy challenges they want to address. When Will the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowships Take Place? Successful host organisations will deliver their Associate Policy Fellowship programmes between January and May 2027 . Policy Fellows must spend a minimum of five days engaging with researchers at the host organisation or organisations during this five-month period. For the standard fellowship model, Fellows or Fellowship teams will spend a minimum of five days in person at a university or universities, with those days distributed across January to May 2027. The programme does not necessarily require Fellows to complete all five days consecutively. Instead, host organisations will need to design a programme that best meets the needs of their Fellows and the policy questions being explored. What Can an Associate Policy Fellowship Include? Each successful host organisation will be responsible for designing a programme that responds appropriately to its Fellows policy needs. Activities may include: 1. Meetings Between Policy Fellows and Researchers Policy Fellows can meet directly with researchers to discuss particular policy questions, challenges or areas where specialist knowledge would be valuable. These engagements may take the form of individual meetings between a Fellow and a researcher or broader interdisciplinary discussions involving researchers from several fields. Roundtable discussions may also be used to bring different academic perspectives to a policy problem. 2. Participation in Relevant Seminars and Events Policy Fellows may participate in seminars, workshops, lectures or other relevant events taking place at the host university or research organisation. This can provide Fellows with additional exposure to emerging research, specialist expertise and wider academic conversations related to their policy responsibilities. 3. Professional and Institutional Network Building Host organisations can use the Fellowship programme to establish stronger connections between participating public and civil servants and the research community. These relationships can help facilitate longer-term knowledge exchange and potentially create future opportunities for collaboration between policymakers and researchers. Who Can Apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards? The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are open to research organisations in the United Kingdom that are eligible for UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) funding . Eligible organisations may include: Universities. Colleges. Research centres. Research institutes. Public sector research establishments. Other eligible independent research organisations. Importantly, organisations do not need previous experience running Policy Fellowships . EvEx specifically encourages applications from organisations that have never previously offered Policy Fellowships, as well as organisations that already have experience delivering similar programmes. Groups of research organisations are also permitted to apply together and jointly operate an Associate Policy Fellowship programme. Do Organisations Need to Have Policy Fellows Identified Before Applying? No. Applicants do not need to know who their prospective Policy Fellows will be when submitting their proposal. Successful organisations can subsequently operate an open application process through which eligible Policy Fellows can apply. The EvEx team can provide support and help amplify these recruitment opportunities. This means organisations interested in establishing a programme should not be discouraged from applying simply because they have not already identified specific public or civil servants to participate. Can Organisations Propose a Specific Fellowship Theme? Yes. Applicants may design their proposed Fellowships around a particular theme or policy topic. However, EvEx advises organisations to consider avoiding themes that are excessively narrow, as broader themes may provide greater flexibility when recruiting Fellows and matching them with appropriate researchers. Organisations uncertain about whether their proposed theme is suitable are encouraged to contact the EvEx team before submitting their application. Who Can Participate as an EvEx Associate Policy Fellow? For this programme, Policy Fellows are UK public and civil servants . Host organisations can recruit individuals from different public bodies and at different levels of seniority. Fellowships may be offered to: Individual public or civil servants. Small teams from the public or civil service. Participants from different public bodies. Participants across different levels of professional seniority. Each Fellow or Fellowship team should engage with researchers for at least five days during the January–May 2027 programme period. Benefits for Successful Host Organisations The programme provides more than financial support. Organisations receiving an EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Award will participate in a dedicated Coaching and Learning Programme designed to support them in developing and delivering effective Policy Fellowship programmes. Successful hosts will receive assistance covering important stages of fellowship delivery. Support From the EvEx Team The EvEx team will provide advice and guidance on designing and delivering a Policy Fellowship programme. Support can cover areas including: Selecting and recruiting Fellows. Matching Policy Fellows with appropriate researchers. Designing fellowship activities. Managing Fellows time within participating institutions. Developing effective approaches to knowledge exchange. Application and Documentation Templates Successful host organisations will receive access to template application forms and other documentation. These resources can be used directly or adapted to suit an organisation s individual recruitment and programme requirements. Coaching and Learning Support Host teams will have access to ongoing assistance from a Coaching and Learning Consultant . This will include: Training. Facilitated workshops. Specially developed shared resources. Practical guidance for Fellowship delivery. Knowledge Exchange Between Host Organisations Successful organisations will also have opportunities to interact with other participating hosts. This provides an additional platform for sharing experiences, exchanging ideas and discussing best practices for running effective Policy Fellowship programmes. Longer-Term Organisational Benefits Running an Associate Policy Fellowship programme can also help participating institutions develop stronger relationships with policymakers and public sector professionals. Potential organisational benefits highlighted by EvEx include: Building networks of public and civil servants. Establishing connections between public sector professionals and researchers. Strengthening institutional policy engagement. Developing the skills of staff responsible for managing Policy Fellowships. Accessing training, workshops and shared learning resources. Creating opportunities to demonstrate case studies and impacts resulting from policy-to-research engagement. Policy Fellows recruited through participating organisations will also be invited to join the wider EvEx Policy Fellows network , through which they can receive invitations to relevant networking activities and events. EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027 Timeline Applicants should take note of the following key dates: 1 September 2026: Applications open. 9 September 2026: Online information session for prospective applicants. 8 October 2026: Application deadline. By 30 October 2026: Applicants expected to be notified of outcomes. Late January 2027: Fellowships begin. March 2027: Interim report submitted. By 31 May 2027: Fellowships completed. 30 June 2027: Final report submitted. The source also lists By 11 January 2026 – EvEx Policy Fellows recruited. This appears chronologically inconsistent with the surrounding 2027 programme dates, so prospective applicants should refer to the official guidance or confirm the intended year directly with EvEx rather than assuming a correction. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards is midday on 8 October 2026 . Applications opened on 1 September 2026 . Applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare their proposals early and carefully review the official guidance before completing the online application. Online Information Session for Applicants EvEx will host an online information session for prospective applicants on: 9 September 2026 at 1:30 p.m. The webinar will provide an opportunity to learn more about the Policy Fellowships and ask questions about either the Fellowship model or the application process. Prospective applicants can register for the session through the official EvEx website. How to Apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Organisations interested in applying should first review the complete programme guidance and application form provided by EvEx. Applicants can then prepare their proposal and submit the final application using the online application form available through the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship webpage . The application guidance and a downloadable application form are available to help organisations prepare their responses before completing the online submission. Applicants are also encouraged to discuss their proposed project with the EvEx team before submitting an application. This provides an opportunity to check whether the proposed organisation and programme meet the scheme s eligibility requirements and intended scope. Applicants wishing to arrange a discussion can contact Christina Rozeik and the EvEx team at evex@csap.cam.ac.uk . Applications may also be submitted in Welsh. Welsh-language guidance is available, and applicants who want the application form in Welsh can request it directly from the EvEx team. APPLY NOW Reporting Requirements for Successful Organisations Successful organisations will be required to report on their Fellowship activities and expenditure at two key stages. Interim Report – March 2027 Around the midpoint of the programme, participating organisations will complete an interim reporting form. The interim report is expected to cover: Information about the EvEx Policy Fellows recruited. Progress achieved to date. Programme activities undertaken. Budget expenditure. Final Report – June 2027 Following completion of the Fellowship programme, host organisations will submit a final report. The report will request fuller information concerning: Delivery of the programme. Overall expenditure. Activities undertaken. Outcomes and impacts that have emerged from the programme. The source states that the final report is due 30 June 2027 . How Many Hosting Awards Are Available? For the 2026–2027 programme , EvEx expects to offer approximately 10 Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards across the United Kingdom . Because the number of awards is limited, eligible organisations interested in participating should carefully develop proposals that demonstrate how their Fellowship programme can create meaningful engagement between researchers and public or civil servants. About Evidence Exchange (EvEx) Evidence Exchange, or EvEx, is supporting stronger connections between research and policymaking through initiatives such as the Associate Policy Fellowship programme. The programme is funded by the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) and delivered by the Centre for Science and Policy (CSaP) at the University of Cambridge , together with partners across the United Kingdom. Through the Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards, EvEx aims to expand Policy Fellowship opportunities beyond its existing consortium and help additional research organisations develop the capacity, expertise and networks required to engage effectively with policymakers. Conclusion The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027 represents a substantial opportunity for UK research organisations seeking to strengthen connections between academic research and public policymaking. With funding of up to £62,500 , successful organisations can establish programmes that bring UK public and civil servants into closer engagement with researchers, creating space to explore real policy challenges, access specialist expertise, develop professional networks and strengthen knowledge exchange. The opportunity is particularly accessible because applicants do not need previous experience running Policy Fellowships, and organisations can receive extensive practical support through EvEx s Coaching and Learning Programme. Universities and other eligible research organisations may also collaborate and submit joint proposals. Approximately 10 hosting awards are expected to be available during the 2026–2027 cycle. Eligible UK research organisations interested in applying should review the official programme guidance, consider attending the 9 September 2026 information session , and prepare their proposal ahead of the final application deadline. Application Deadline: Midday, 8 October 2026. Visit the OFY website for more Grant and Fellowship opportunities. title: Call for Youth Researchers: Apply to Support Youth Participation and Policy Research Under the Youth Voice Naija Project
summary: The Network of Youth for Sustainable Initiative (NGYouthSDGs) has opened a call for Youth Researchers to support field research, youth engagement, interviews, data collection and documentation under the Youth Voice Naija Project . This opportunity is designed for young people who are passionate about research, youth participation, public policy and inclusive decision-making and who are willing to work directly with young people whose voices are often missing from formal policy and decision-making processes. Through the project, selected Youth Researchers will contribute to efforts aimed at strengthening the participation and leadership of underrepresented young people and creating meaningful opportunities for them to contribute to the development, implementation and monitoring of the National Youth Policy 2026–2030 . If you are a young person interested in research and community engagement and are motivated to help ensure that young people s experiences and perspectives are represented in policy processes, this call may provide an opportunity to gain practical research experience while contributing to an important youth-focused initiative. About the Youth Voice Naija Project The Youth Voice Naija Project focuses on increasing the meaningful participation of young people in policy and decision-making spaces. Young people represent an important part of society, but not all youth have equal opportunities to participate in discussions and processes that affect their lives. Some groups face barriers related to geography, socioeconomic circumstances, access to information, limited representation or other forms of exclusion. As a result, policy processes can sometimes fail to adequately capture the experiences and priorities of young people who are most difficult to reach. The Youth Voice Naija Project seeks to address this challenge by supporting greater participation from underrepresented and often-overlooked youth groups . A key focus of the project is enabling young people to directly engage in processes related to the National Youth Policy 2026–2030 . By collecting young people s perspectives and documenting their experiences, the initiative aims to contribute to more inclusive youth policy processes. The Youth Researchers recruited through this call will therefore play an important role in connecting the project with young people in selected communities and locations. What Will Youth Researchers Do? Selected Youth Researchers will support several aspects of the project s field research and youth engagement activities. Their responsibilities will focus on reaching young people, collecting information, conducting engagements and ensuring that the experiences and perspectives shared by participants are properly documented. Key activities may include: 1. Participant Outreach Youth Researchers will help identify and reach potential participants for the project s research and engagement activities. This is particularly important because the project is interested in reaching young people who may not normally have access to policy discussions or youth participation opportunities. Researchers may therefore be expected to: Identify relevant youth groups and individuals. Connect with young people within selected communities and locations. Encourage eligible young people to participate in research activities. Communicate information about the research process to potential participants. Help ensure that underrepresented youth groups are adequately reached. Support inclusive participation throughout the research process. The ability to communicate respectfully with different groups of young people will therefore be important. 2. Field Data Collection Youth Researchers will participate in collecting information from young people in selected locations. The information gathered may help the project understand young people s: Experiences; Challenges; Priorities; Aspirations; Views on youth participation; Perspectives on policy processes; Capacity-building needs; and Experiences with decision-making and leadership opportunities. Researchers will be expected to approach data collection responsibly and accurately, ensuring that information gathered from participants is properly recorded and documented. 3. One-on-One Engagements With Young People The opportunity specifically involves one-on-one engagements with young people. These interactions can provide participants with space to share their individual experiences and perspectives in greater depth. Youth Researchers may be required to engage participants through structured conversations or interviews and capture relevant information arising from those discussions. Strong listening and interpersonal communication skills can therefore be valuable for anyone interested in applying. 4. Interviews Youth Researchers will also support interviews with young people. Through interviews, the project can gather detailed information about the realities facing young people, particularly those whose experiences may not be adequately reflected in mainstream policy discussions. Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating with people from different backgrounds and asking questions in a respectful and appropriate manner. 5. Documentation Another important responsibility will be documenting the experiences and perspectives of participating young people. Accurate documentation can help transform individual experiences into useful research findings that can inform youth participation and policy processes. Researchers should consequently be: Detail-oriented; Responsible; Organized; Accurate when recording information; and Committed to representing participants views fairly. Research Training for Selected Applicants Selected Youth Researchers will participate in a Research Training before supporting data collection across the selected locations. The training is intended to prepare researchers for their responsibilities and help create a common understanding of the project s research and data-collection processes. Participation in the training is particularly important because field research requires researchers to understand how to interact with participants, collect information appropriately and document findings consistently. The training may therefore help selected researchers develop or strengthen practical skills relevant to: Field research; Data collection; Interviewing; Youth engagement; Documentation; Community outreach; and Research ethics and responsible engagement. For young people seeking to build practical experience in research, public policy, youth development or community engagement, participation in such training can also provide useful professional exposure. Who Is NGYouthSDGs Looking For? The organization is looking for young people who demonstrate a genuine interest in research, youth participation and policy processes . According to the call, successful applicants should be: Curious and interested in learning; Responsible in carrying out assigned responsibilities; Willing to engage directly with young people; Interested in research and data collection; Comfortable reaching out to youth groups and individuals; Willing to support field research activities; Interested in youth participation and policy processes; and Prepared to work with young people in communities and locations that are often overlooked. An applicant does not simply need to be interested in research in theory. The opportunity requires a willingness to participate in practical activities involving outreach, interviews, data collection and documentation. Why This Opportunity May Be Valuable for Young Researchers Participating as a Youth Researcher can provide practical exposure to the intersection of research, youth development and public policy . Unlike opportunities that are primarily classroom-based, this role involves engaging directly with young people and gathering information from communities. Some of the potential benefits include: Practical Research Experience Researchers will gain practical exposure to field research activities, including participant outreach, interviews, data collection and documentation. This can be particularly useful for young people interested in careers or further study in: Social sciences; Development studies; Public policy; International development; Governance; Political science; Sociology; Youth development; Community development; Research and evaluation; and Related fields. title: Why Municipal Youth Participation? European Training Seminar 2026 in Budapest, Hungary
summary: The Why Municipal Youth Participation? seminar is an international training and professional development opportunity designed for people working to strengthen youth participation in local and regional decision-making . The seminar will bring together 50 participants in Budapest, Hungary, to explore practical approaches to municipal youth participation and the implementation of the new European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life . Organized by the Council of Europe Youth Department , within the framework of the Youth Revitalising Democracy project, together with the Democracy Reloading Partnership of Erasmus+ national agencies , the seminar will take place from 16 to 21 November 2026 at the European Youth Centre Budapest . The training is particularly relevant for municipal youth policy officers, youth policy practitioners, locally elected political representatives, youth councils, and youth civil society organizations involved in developing or implementing local and regional youth participation policies. Applications must be submitted by 15 September 2026 at 24:00 UTC . Who Can Apply? The seminar is primarily intended for: Municipal youth policy officers and their local partners Locally elected political representatives Local youth councils Youth civil society organizations Youth leaders Youth policy makers Youth policy officers Other practitioners involved in planning and implementing local or regional youth participation policies and practices Applicants must generally: Be resident and working in a Council of Europe member state , although exceptions may be possible when duly justified. Be able to communicate independently in English . Be actively engaged in youth participation policy or practice at the local or regional level. Priority will be given to participants from countries participating in the Democracy Reloading Partnership , although participation is not exclusively limited to those countries. No specific race, ethnicity, gender, or academic qualification requirement is stated in the provided information. What Is the “Why Municipal Youth Participation?” Seminar? The Why Municipal Youth Participation? seminar is designed to strengthen the capacity of local and regional actors to develop and implement meaningful youth participation policies. Youth participation is an important part of democratic life because local and regional authorities make decisions that directly affect young people and their communities. The seminar provides participants with an opportunity to learn about European standards for youth participation, exchange experiences with peers, explore practical tools, and examine examples of municipal youth participation in Budapest. The event will bring together 50 participants for an intensive learning and exchange experience. Who Organizes the Seminar? The seminar is organized by the Council of Europe Youth Department as part of the Youth Revitalising Democracy project. It is being organized in cooperation with the Democracy Reloading Partnership of Erasmus+ national agencies . The Council of Europe is a major European intergovernmental organization focused on human rights, democracy, and the rule of law. The cooperation between the Council of Europe and Democracy Reloading gives the seminar a particular focus on strengthening democratic participation at the local level. Where and When Will the Training Take Place? The seminar will take place in: European Youth Centre Budapest Budapest, Hungary Dates 16–21 November 2026 Participants are expected to arrive on Monday, 16 November and can leave on Saturday, 21 November 2026 . The activity will therefore provide several days of face-to-face learning, discussion, networking, and practical exploration of municipal youth participation. Main Aim of the Seminar The central aim is to support local and regional municipalities in designing and implementing participative youth policies that align with the new European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life. Participants will have the opportunity to explore how European-level standards can be translated into practical approaches within their own municipalities and communities. The seminar is therefore not only about learning theoretical concepts. It is also focused on understanding how youth participation can work in practice at the local level. The European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life A major focus of the seminar is the European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life . The Charter is described in the opportunity information as the key standard for youth participation at local and regional level. The Charter was first adopted in 1992 and subsequently underwent a major revision during 2024–2025 . More than 400 stakeholders participated in the revision process. According to the provided information, the revised Charter was adopted by the Congress of Local and Regional Authorities and the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe in 2026 . The Council of Europe and its partners at international, national, and local levels are taking measures to support implementation of the Charter s provisions. This seminar is part of that broader effort. Why Is the European Charter Important for the Seminar? The Charter provides a framework for youth participation at local and regional levels. The seminar will help participants become familiar with its provisions and consider how those provisions can be implemented in their own local realities. Participants can therefore explore questions such as: How can young people participate meaningfully in local decision-making? What mechanisms can municipalities use to involve young people? How can local youth policies become more participatory? How can youth councils and civil society contribute to local policymaking? How can European standards be translated into practical municipal policies? What approaches have worked in different communities? The seminar provides a setting for participants to explore these issues collectively. Objectives of the Seminar The training has several specific objectives. 1. Understanding the New European Charter Participants will become familiar with the provisions of the new European Charter on the Participation of Young People in Local and Regional Life . They will also explore ways to apply those provisions within their own local and regional contexts. This means participants can move from simply knowing about the Charter to considering how it can inform practical youth participation policies. 2. Understanding Council of Europe Standards Participants will learn about Council of Europe standards for local youth participation in democratic life . This can help practitioners understand the broader European framework surrounding youth participation and democratic engagement. 3. Understanding Democracy Reloading The seminar will introduce participants to the Democracy Reloading concept and its tools . These tools are intended to support municipal youth participation in decision-making. This component can provide participants with practical resources that they can potentially use within their own municipalities and youth policy work. 4. Sharing Experiences and Practices Another important objective is peer learning . Participants will have the opportunity to share their experiences and practices with other people working on youth participation. This creates space for participants to learn not only from trainers but also from colleagues working in different countries and local contexts. 5. Learning From Budapest Participants will also gain insight into practices of municipal youth participation in Budapest and its district municipalities . This practical component allows participants to examine how youth participation operates in a real municipal environment. What Will the Program Include? The seminar will include several learning and practical components. Introduction to Council of Europe Youth Participation Standards Participants will be introduced to key standards developed by the Council of Europe concerning youth participation. Democracy Reloading Concept and Tools The program will introduce the Democracy Reloading approach and tools designed to support municipal youth participation. Visits to Local Practices in Budapest Participants will have the opportunity to visit local examples of municipal youth participation in Budapest. Council of Europe and Democracy Reloading Resources The seminar will present relevant tools and resources from both the Council of Europe and the Democracy Reloading Partnership. Together, these elements combine theoretical learning, practical examples, peer exchange, and exposure to useful resources. Who Is the Seminar Recommended For? The training overview specifically recommends the opportunity for: Youth leaders Youth policy makers Youth policy officers The broader expected participant profile includes municipal youth policy officers, local partners, elected representatives, youth councils, and youth civil society actors who are actively involved in youth participation policies and practices. The key point is that applicants should have a relevant connection to local or regional youth participation . Eligible Countries and Regions The training overview identifies participants from a broad group of European and neighboring countries. These include: Other Eligible Countries Andorra Monaco Morocco San Marino Tunisia United Kingdom Eastern Partnership Countries Armenia Azerbaijan Belarus Georgia Moldova Ukraine Erasmus+ Youth Programme Countries Austria Belgium Bulgaria Croatia Cyprus Czech Republic Denmark Estonia Finland France Germany Greece Hungary Iceland Ireland Italy Latvia Liechtenstein Lithuania Luxembourg Malta Netherlands Norway Poland Portugal Republic of North Macedonia Romania Serbia Slovak Republic Slovenia Spain Sweden Switzerland Türkiye Western Balkan Countries Albania Bosnia and Herzegovina Kosovo Montenegro The training information notes that priority will be given to participants from partner countries of the Democracy Reloading Partnership, but participation is not exclusively limited to those countries . English Language Requirement The working language of the seminar is English . Participants are expected to be able to communicate independently in English . Applicants should therefore be comfortable participating in discussions, following presentations, interacting with other participants, and engaging in group activities in English. No Participation Fee There is no participation fee foreseen for selected participants. Participants are pre-selected by the relevant Erasmus+ national agencies and SALTOs . This means prospective participants should pay attention to the application and selection arrangements associated with their country or sending organization. Accommodation and Meals Accommodation and meals will be provided by the Council of Europe at the European Youth Centre Budapest . Meals will be provided from: Dinner on Monday through breakfast on Saturday. This covers the main period of the seminar from arrival on 16 November through departure on 21 November. Travel Reimbursement Participants are expected to arrive on Monday, 16 November and can depart on Saturday, 21 November . Information about travel reimbursement should be obtained from the participant s Erasmus+ national agency or SALTO Centre . Prospective applicants should therefore contact the appropriate national agency or SALTO Centre if they need clarification about eligible travel expenses and reimbursement arrangements. Youthpass Certificate Participants are entitled to receive a Youthpass certificate from the organizer. Youthpass is used to recognize and document competence development gained through participation in youth activities and learning experiences. For participants, this can provide formal recognition of the learning and competencies developed during the seminar. Application Deadline The application deadline is: 15 September 2026 at 24:00 UTC Applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline. Because the selection process takes place before the seminar, applicants should not wait until the final hours to prepare and submit their applications. Selection Date The stated date of selection is 28 September 2026 . Applicants should therefore expect the selection process to take place after the application deadline and before the November seminar. Meals Meals are provided from dinner on Monday through breakfast on Saturday. Travel Travel reimbursement arrangements should be confirmed with the relevant Erasmus+ national agency or SALTO Centre. Youthpass Participants are entitled to receive a Youthpass certificate recognizing their competence development during the activity. How the Seminar Can Benefit Youth Policy Practitioners The seminar is particularly valuable for people who are already involved in youth participation at municipal or regional level. Participants can benefit from: Greater familiarity with European youth participation standards Better understanding of the revised European Charter Exposure to Democracy Reloading tools Opportunities to exchange practices with international peers Exposure to municipal youth participation practices in Budapest Access to relevant Council of Europe resources Access to Democracy Reloading resources Professional networking with other youth policy practitioners Recognition of competence development through Youthpass The combination of learning, practice-sharing, and networking can help participants take new ideas back to their municipalities or organizations. Why Municipal Youth Participation Matters Local governments make decisions concerning many aspects of young people s lives. Effective youth participation can provide mechanisms through which young people can contribute to decisions affecting their communities. For youth policy practitioners, understanding how to create meaningful participation structures can therefore be an important part of developing effective local youth policies. The seminar approaches this issue from a European perspective, using the Council of Europe s standards and the new European Charter as important reference points. How to Prepare for the Application Prospective applicants can strengthen their preparation by clearly understanding the focus of the seminar. Before applying, consider: Your current role Be clear about how your work relates to youth policy, youth participation, municipal decision-making, youth councils, or youth civil society. Your experience Identify practical examples of your involvement in local or regional youth participation. Your motivation Think about why you want to develop your knowledge of municipal youth participation. Your municipality or organization Consider the youth participation challenges your municipality or organization currently faces. What you can contribute Since the seminar emphasizes sharing experiences and practices, think about examples and lessons that you can contribute to discussions with other participants. Your language ability Make sure you are comfortable communicating independently in English. For this reason, applicants should contact the organizers directly for the latest information before making final arrangements. The listed contact person is: Laszlo Foldi Email: laszlo.foldi@cfwb.be Telephone: +32 2 210 52 33 Key Takeaways The Why Municipal Youth Participation? seminar provides a focused learning opportunity for professionals and youth participation actors who want to strengthen local and regional youth participation. The most important details are: It is a seminar and training opportunity . It will take place in Budapest, Hungary . The dates are 16–21 November 2026 . 50 participants will take part. title: Tara’s Circle 2026 Global Open Call Offers €100,000 to Women-Led Impact Projects
summary: Applications are open for Tara’s Circle 2026, an international initiative supporting women-led projects that generate measurable social, environmental or economic impact. Organised by Tara for Women, the 2026 programme will distribute up to €100,000 among 15 winning projects across five thematic areas. Within each area, three projects will receive cash support of €10,000, €6,000 or €4,000. In addition to the financial support, all 15 winners will enter a six-month development programme offering strategic mentoring, specialised training, international visibility, networking opportunities and potential connections with investors. The call is open to women aged 18 and above from any country. Applicants must be founders or co-founders of their projects and play an active leadership role. Eligible projects should be at the seed, defined minimum viable product or functional minimum viable product stage and demonstrate the potential to become sustainable and scalable. Applications must be submitted by September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central European Summer Time. This is a midday deadline rather than an end-of-day deadline, so applicants should carefully convert it to their local time. All information is based on the official Tara’s Circle 2026 Open Call Guidelines . Tara’s Circle 2026 at a Glance Call detail Information Organiser Tara for Women Programme Tara’s Circle 2026 Geographic scope International Eligible applicants Women aged 18 or older Leadership requirement Woman founder or co-founder actively leading the project Project stages Seed, defined MVP or functional MVP Thematic areas Five Total award allocation Up to €100,000 Number of winning projects 15 First place in each area €10,000 Second place in each area €6,000 Third place in each area €4,000 Additional support Six-month support programme Application languages English and Spanish Application opening date July 1, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. CEST Application deadline September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. CEST Finalist notification October 14, 2026 Awards ceremony November 18, 2026 Application method Online application form only About Tara for Women Tara for Women is a Spanish nonprofit foundation with a global mission to advance women’s talent and help women and girls develop projects capable of creating sustainable impact. The foundation supports women through: Project financing Individual and strategic mentorship Professional training International visibility Access to networks Entrepreneurship support Partnerships and collaboration opportunities Connections with members of the investment ecosystem Its work is organised around education and entrepreneurship, with an emphasis on sustainability, inclusion, empowerment, transparency and measurable social impact. The foundation seeks to address the barriers that prevent women from turning ideas into sustainable projects. Its initiatives are designed to provide women with the financing, confidence, knowledge and professional relationships required to grow their projects and contribute to positive change. More information about the foundation’s mission and values is available on the official Tara for Women website . Purpose of Tara’s Circle 2026 Tara’s Circle 2026 supports women-led projects that combine innovation with a clear social, environmental or economic purpose. The programme is not limited to one industry or type of business. Applicants may propose commercial ventures, social enterprises, technology projects, cultural initiatives, educational models, healthcare solutions, sustainability projects or other ventures that fit within the five thematic areas. The programme seeks projects that demonstrate: A clearly identified problem A relevant and innovative solution Meaningful social, environmental or economic impact A capable and committed team Potential to become financially sustainable Capacity to scale or expand A defined or operating minimum viable product A coherent business or operating model Measurable outcomes Alignment with one or more programme themes The emphasis is on women-led initiatives that can move beyond a general idea and demonstrate how their proposed solution could be implemented, sustained and expanded. Who Can Apply? Applicants must satisfy the following main conditions: Be a woman aged 18 or older when the application is submitted. Be the founder or co-founder of the project. Play an active role in leading the project. Submit a project with national or international scope. Have a project at an eligible development stage. Demonstrate a commitment to creating social, environmental or economic impact. Show potential for scalability and long-term sustainability. Submit all required documents through the official platform before the deadline. Projects may be based in any country. No geographic or nationality restriction is stated. The application may be submitted by a woman working with a wider team, provided she is a founder or co-founder and remains actively involved in project leadership. Women-Led Project Requirement A project is considered women-led when a woman: Founded or co-founded the initiative Participates actively in strategic decision-making Exercises a genuine leadership role Is substantially involved in developing and implementing the project Is not included merely as a nominal or symbolic founder Applicants should explain their position, responsibilities and decision-making role clearly in the application and pitch deck. Projects that include men or other team members are not automatically excluded. The essential condition is that an eligible woman founder or co-founder actively leads the initiative. International Eligibility Tara’s Circle 2026 is open to applicants worldwide. Projects may operate: Within one country Across multiple countries Regionally Internationally Through physical operations Through digital or hybrid models No citizenship, nationality, racial or continental restriction is published. However, international eligibility does not guarantee that the foundation can transfer cash to every country. Financial disbursement remains subject to applicable laws, banking mechanisms, international regulations and sanctions. Cash Awards and Funding Structure Each of the five thematic areas receives a total cash allocation of €20,000. The amount is distributed among three winning projects in each thematic area: Placement Amount per winner First place €10,000 Second place €6,000 Third place €4,000 Total per thematic area €20,000 Across all five thematic areas, the programme plans to provide: Five first-place awards worth €10,000 each Five second-place awards worth €6,000 each Five third-place awards worth €4,000 each Fifteen awards in total Up to €100,000 in total financial support The funding is non-repayable, subject to the applicable terms, agreements, tax rules and transfer restrictions. International Funding Restrictions Although applications are accepted internationally, the transfer of funding is subject to legal and operational conditions. Tara for Women states that it may postpone, restrict or cancel a financial transfer if payment is prevented by: Applicable laws or regulations International sanctions Banking restrictions Lack of a safe or lawful payment mechanism Force majeure Other conditions outside the foundation’s control If financial support cannot be transferred, Tara for Women may consider providing an alternative form of non-financial assistance where appropriate. International applicants should therefore understand that being selected does not override banking laws, sanctions or other transfer restrictions. The Five Thematic Areas Applicants may submit their project under one or more thematic areas, provided that the selection is consistent with the project’s activities, impact model and objectives. The categories are indicative rather than exhaustive. Cross-cutting and hybrid projects may still qualify. 1. Sustainability, Environment and Mobility This area seeks projects contributing to a more sustainable, resilient and environmentally responsible future. Relevant projects may address: Circular economy models Waste reduction and waste valorisation Recycling and material recovery Clean and renewable energy Energy efficiency Decarbonisation Sustainable transport Low-emission mobility Climate adaptation Community climate resilience Carbon capture Carbon reduction and compensation Biodiversity conservation Ecosystem protection and restoration Efficient resource management Environmental technology Sustainable urban systems Projects should explain the environmental problem being addressed, the measurable benefit of the solution and how the model can be sustained or expanded. 2. Health and Well-Being This area supports projects that improve physical, mental or social well-being while expanding fair and inclusive access to healthcare. Special consideration is given to women’s health and caregiving. Relevant initiatives may include: Preventive healthcare Community-based health services Mental health support Emotional well-being Women’s health across different stages of life Maternal or reproductive health Caregiving products and services New models of care delivery Healthcare-access solutions Technology supporting health services Projects reducing inequalities in access to care Community health education Affordable health-related products Applicants should demonstrate how their project responds to a real health need and why their approach can improve access, quality, equity or outcomes. 3. Social Innovation, Education and Community Development This thematic area supports projects that strengthen communities through education, inclusion, entrepreneurship and new economic opportunities. Relevant initiatives may address: Social entrepreneurship Community-led innovation Support for underserved communities Solutions for vulnerable populations Inclusive and accessible education Quality education Workforce development Entrepreneurship training Employment creation Social inclusion Economic inclusion Digital inclusion Skills development Innovative economic models Projects generating measurable community impact Applicants should explain how the proposed model will create meaningful, lasting benefits rather than temporary or unmeasurable activities. 4. Technology and Science This area supports projects with a substantial technological or scientific foundation. Eligible initiatives may involve: Digital platforms Software products Mobile applications Artificial intelligence Data analytics Automation Cloud computing Emerging technologies Technology for healthcare Educational technology Climate and sustainability technology Inclusion-focused technology Digital economic-development tools Technology improving access or efficiency Productivity tools Digital impact-measurement systems Scalable technology with measurable social or environmental value Projects should demonstrate that technology is a meaningful part of the solution rather than an unnecessary feature added only to appear innovative. Applicants should explain: How the technology works Which users need it What makes it different How it will be developed How it will generate or support revenue How it can scale How its impact will be measured What ethical or data-protection issues may arise 5. Design, Culture and Impact-Driven Fashion This area focuses on creativity as a means of generating positive social, environmental or economic change. Relevant projects may include: Sustainable fashion Circular fashion Responsible production Ethical supply chains Design responding to social challenges Design addressing environmental problems Cultural projects with measurable community value Creative industries Projects preserving cultural heritage Initiatives protecting traditional knowledge Innovative cultural-production models New approaches to cultural consumption Inclusive design Responsible material use Creative merit alone is not enough. Projects should demonstrate how their design, cultural or fashion model produces measurable impact and can remain economically or operationally sustainable. Applying Under More Than One Area Projects may be submitted under one or more thematic areas. A project combining health and technology, for example, may have a legitimate connection to both categories. Similarly, a circular-fashion initiative may fit under sustainability and impact-driven fashion. Applicants should select multiple categories only where there is a clear and defensible connection. The application should remain coherent and should not be stretched artificially to fit every available theme. The declared thematic area is one part of the evaluation but does not independently determine whether a project will be selected. Eligible Project Stages The call supports projects that have progressed beyond a vague or completely untested concept. Three development stages are described. Seed-Stage Projects These are early-stage initiatives with significant growth potential. They may have the following characteristics: The product or service is still under development. The underlying business idea has already been validated. The project is seeking initial external funding. Potential funding sources may include angel investors, incubators or seed funds. The founding team is being formed or strengthened. The project has begun defining how its solution will work. A seed-stage applicant should still provide evidence that the problem and proposed solution have been investigated and validated. Defined MVP Stage A minimum viable product, or MVP, is the simplest workable version of a product or service that can be tested with users. At the defined MVP stage: The project has moved beyond the general idea phase. The value proposition is clear. A functional MVP design exists. Essential features have been identified. The team is actively developing the MVP. The product is not yet fully operational. Applicants should show that they understand what must be built, who will use it and what must be tested. Functional MVP Stage At this stage: An operational and demonstrable MVP already exists. The product or service has been tested with real users. The project has received initial market or user feedback. The team is ready to improve or scale the model. The founders are prepared to receive mentoring and financial support. The project can demonstrate early evidence of relevance or demand. Projects that are only abstract ideas without validation, a defined solution or meaningful development work are unlikely to meet the published stage requirements. Six-Month Support Programme for Winners The 15 winning projects will receive access to a comprehensive six-month development programme. The support is intended to strengthen the founders’ capabilities, improve project visibility and accelerate sustainable growth. Strategic Mentoring Winners will have access to personalised mentoring from professionals connected to entrepreneurship, technology and social impact. Mentoring may focus on: Strengthening the business model Refining the growth strategy Improving founder leadership Identifying operational weaknesses Developing measurable objectives Planning for expansion Clarifying financial priorities Preparing for partnerships or investment Visibility and Positioning Winning projects may be promoted through: Media coverage Social media Tara for Women’s platforms Partner events Strategic networks Entrepreneurship and impact platforms The objective is to increase public awareness of the projects and create new opportunities for collaboration. Specialised Training Winners will receive access to training in areas such as: Innovation Leadership Sustainability Artificial intelligence Product development Commercial strategy Fundraising Training may be delivered virtually, in person or through a combination of formats. Networking and Partnerships The six-month programme will create opportunities to connect with: Entrepreneurs Investors Companies Public and private institutions Mentors Experts Other women founders Potential strategic partners These relationships may help winners identify clients, collaborators, advisers, investors or implementation partners. Financial Support Each winning project will receive the cash amount corresponding to its placement. The funding may be used for activities such as: Technology development Product improvement Marketing Talent recruitment Commercial expansion Operational strengthening Market testing Other approved project-development needs Applicants should provide a specific and credible explanation of how the requested capital will be used. Potential Investor Connections Winners may be introduced to investment networks associated with Tara for Women. Potential connections may include: Business angels Seed funds Accelerators Impact investors Other organisations interested in women-led projects The programme will also help participants communicate their value propositions more clearly to investors and other members of the entrepreneurship ecosystem. Investor introductions do not guarantee that a project will receive additional investment. Special and Corporate Awards Through partnerships, Tara for Women may add special awards or corporate recognitions. Any additional recognition must remain consistent with the programme’s objectives and may not change the basic eligibility conditions, evaluation criteria or core allocation of funding within each thematic area. How to Apply Applications must be submitted digitally through an official form. Applicants can choose between: Official English application form Official Spanish application form Applications submitted by email, social media or any other method will not be accepted. Applicants should use only one official form and ensure that every required field and attachment is complete. Mandatory Application Materials Applicants must submit: A completed online application form A complete pitch deck in PDF format An elevator-pitch video lasting no more than two minutes Any additional documentation requested through the application platform All information must remain consistent across the form, pitch deck, video and supporting materials. Conflicting financial figures, project descriptions, team information or impact claims may weaken an application or raise verification concerns. Pitch Deck Requirements The pitch deck must present the project clearly, concisely and attractively. It should include the following elements. Project Summary Explain: What the project does Why it matters The project’s purpose The overall vision The intended impact The summary should capture attention quickly and provide a clear introduction to the project. Problem Describe the specific need, challenge or pain point being addressed. Applicants should include: Relevant data Evidence Examples User experiences Market information Community needs Other information showing that the problem is real and important The problem should be specific enough to understand and significant enough to justify the proposed solution. Solution Present the product or service as a response to the problem. Explain: How the solution works What users receive Why the approach is effective What value it creates What makes it practical How it differs from existing approaches Business Model Explain how the project currently generates or plans to generate revenue. This may include: Product sales Subscriptions Annual licences Service fees Partnerships Institutional contracts Training Customisation services Other revenue streams The business-model section should address: Revenue sources Pricing Sales channels Customer-acquisition channels Major operating costs Financial sustainability Examples of potential expenses include software development, cloud infrastructure, personnel, sales, marketing, regulatory compliance and legal support. Target Market Identify: The intended customer or beneficiary Customer profile Market segment Geographic market Estimated market size Growth potential Demand for the solution Applicants should distinguish between users, beneficiaries, customers and paying clients where these groups are different. Competitive Advantage Explain what makes the project different or better than available alternatives. Competitive advantages may relate to: Technology Intellectual property Delivery model Specialist expertise Partnerships Cost Accessibility Impact Cultural relevance Speed or efficiency User experience Claims should be supported by evidence rather than broad statements that the project is unique. Team Introduce the key people involved in the initiative. Include: Names Roles Responsibilities Relevant experience Professional or technical capabilities Reasons the team is qualified to implement the project The woman founder or co-founder’s active leadership should be clear. Financial Projections Provide realistic estimates of: Revenue Expenses Growth Funding needs Financial sustainability Projections should cover the next one to three years. The figures do not need to be exact, but they should be internally consistent and connected to the project’s operating and business model. Investment Requirements State: How much funding the project needs What the funding will be used for How the investment will advance the project What results or impact the investment is expected to produce Possible uses include technology development, hiring, marketing, market expansion, product testing or other clearly justified activities. Elevator-Pitch Requirements Applicants must submit a video pitch lasting no more than two minutes. The video should explain: Who the founder is What the project does What problem it addresses Why the problem matters How the proposed solution works What makes the solution distinctive Who the target market is What support, investment or partnerships are needed The objective is to create immediate interest among potential investors, partners, mentors or customers. The video must be uploaded to a public platform, specifically YouTube, and shared through an unrestricted link. Applicants should ensure that: The video is publicly accessible or unlisted with unrestricted link access. No password or permission request is required. The link works correctly. The video remains available until the call closes. The presentation does not exceed two minutes. The audio is clear. The main value proposition is communicated quickly. Online Registration Form The online form includes sections concerning: Legal and Contact Information Applicants may be asked to provide: Full name Email address Telephone number Role in the project Legal name of the entity Address Project logo Other organisational information Impact Applicants must explain the project’s contribution to social, environmental or economic impact and its relationship with the Sustainable Development Goals. Formal SDG alignment is used as an evaluation and partnership framework, but the call does not state that applicants must satisfy a separate SDG certification requirement. Ethics Applicants must provide information about relevant ethical issues, including: Use of personal or project data Use of biological materials, if applicable Research or experimentation Privacy Other ethical considerations connected to the project Commitment Statement Applicants must confirm: The truthfulness of the information submitted Their commitment to participate The absence of conflicts of interest Acceptance of the programme’s terms Evaluation Criteria Eligible applications will be assessed by an expert committee and, where applicable, a jury. The evaluation is structured around four dimensions. Impact Evaluators will consider: The relevance of the problem Potential social, environmental or economic benefit Reach of the proposed impact Depth of impact Alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals Coherence between the solution and intended results Implementation Capacity This dimension considers whether the team can execute the proposed project. Evaluators may examine: Founder and co-founder experience Founder involvement Team structure Complementary capabilities Available resources Planned resources Coherence between objectives and implementation capacity Excellence The excellence assessment covers the project’s overall quality. This includes: Level of innovation Clarity of objectives Strength of the value proposition Viability of the model Quality appropriate to the project’s development stage Internal consistency of the application Thematic Fit The committee will assess how well the project fits the thematic area under which it is submitted. Hybrid projects are not automatically excluded. However, applicants must explain the relationship between the project and each selected theme. Selection Process The selection process includes the following stages: 1. Eligibility Review The foundation verifies whether: The applicant meets the participation requirements. The project is women-led. The applicant is at least 18. The project is at an eligible development stage. All required documents have been submitted. Links and files are accessible. 2. Technical Evaluation Eligible projects are evaluated comparatively by an expert committee using the published assessment criteria. 3. Finalist Selection Selected projects advance to the finalist stage. Finalist status does not guarantee receipt of an award. 4. Jury Presentation Finalists present their projects to a jury. The jury may: Ask questions Request explanations Challenge assumptions Seek clarification about finances, impact or implementation Examine the founder’s understanding of the project 5. Winner Selection The jury chooses three winning projects within each thematic area. Awards are allocated according to first, second and third place. 6. Public Announcement Winners will be announced through the programme’s official channels according to the published calendar. Important Dates Stage Date Applications opened July 1, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. CEST Application deadline September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. CEST Fifteen finalists notified October 14, 2026 Tara’s Circle Awards Ceremony November 18, 2026 The deadline is 12:00 noon CEST, equivalent to 10:00 a.m. UTC. Applicants should calculate the corresponding time in their own country and avoid assuming they can submit until midnight. Legal Conditions By submitting an application, participants accept the programme’s terms. Selected applicants may be required to: Provide additional information Sign a confidentiality agreement Sign an image-consent agreement Allow the project to be featured on the foundation’s website and social media Sign a collaboration agreement Confirm their entitlement to receive the funding Comply with applicable tax and legal requirements For individuals or self-employed recipients, the funding is subject to the applicable 19% tax withholding described in the official guidelines. Applicants should obtain independent tax or legal advice if they are uncertain about the treatment of an international award in their country. Incomplete Applications and Broken Links Incomplete applications or submissions containing inaccessible links will be considered ineligible. Applicants should verify that: The pitch deck opens correctly. The PDF is not corrupted. The video link works. The video does not require approval to view. All information is consistent. Required files remain online until the deadline. Contact information is accurate. The application form has been fully completed. Applicants should check all links in a private or incognito browser window before submission to confirm that reviewers can access them without using the applicant’s account. Technical Support Questions concerning the application process should be sent to: info@taraforwomen.org This is the only official support channel. The foundation states that: Questions sent through social media will not be answered. Questions sent through personal communication channels will not be answered. Responses will normally be provided within a maximum of two business days. Requests submitted during the final 48 hours before the deadline will not be addressed. Applicants requiring clarification should therefore contact the foundation well before September 15, 2026. Recommendations for a Strong Application Applicants should: Read the full guidelines before beginning. Confirm eligibility before preparing the submission. Select the most appropriate thematic area. Prepare the pitch deck in advance. Keep project information consistent across all materials. Use reliable evidence to explain the problem. Define the target market clearly. Explain how revenue will be generated. Provide realistic financial projections. Demonstrate the woman founder’s active leadership. Show measurable impact and scalability. State exactly how the funding would be used. Keep the two-minute pitch clear and memorable. Test all links before submission. Submit well before the deadline. Conclusion Tara’s Circle 2026 offers women founders worldwide an opportunity to secure financial support, mentoring, visibility, specialised training, networking and potential investor connections. The programme will distribute up to €100,000 among 15 women-led projects across sustainability, health, social innovation, technology, science, design, culture and impact-driven fashion. Five first-place projects will receive €10,000 each, five second-place projects will receive €6,000 each and five third-place projects will receive €4,000 each. All winners will also join a six-month support programme intended to strengthen their leadership, business models and growth strategies. Applicants must be women aged 18 or older who founded or co-founded and actively lead an eligible project. Initiatives may come from any country but should be at the seed, defined MVP or functional MVP stage and demonstrate meaningful impact, scalability and sustainability. Applications must include a completed online form, a PDF pitch deck and an elevator-pitch video of no more than two minutes. The deadline is September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. CEST. Interested applicants should study the official guidelines carefully, prepare all documents in advance and submit through the official English or Spanish application form before the deadline.
