title: STARLIGHT 2.0: Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe | Applications Open
summary: Across Europe, democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights continue to face significant pressure. The EU Charter of Fundamental Rights provides an important legal framework for protecting these rights, but its potential as a tool for strategic litigation remains underused. STARLIGHT 2.0 – Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe is now accepting applications from legal professionals who want to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights to pursue systemic change and improve rights protection across Europe. The programme brings together legal training, practical skills development, mentorship, legal clinics and networking opportunities to help participants turn strategic litigation into a tool for lasting impact. The programme is delivered by Democracy Reporting International, the Hertie School and the Hungarian Helsinki Committee , with support from the European Commission s CERV programme. About STARLIGHT 2.0 STARLIGHT 2.0 is designed for legal professionals who already have experience in litigation and want to develop stronger knowledge and practical strategies for using the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights in strategic cases. The programme focuses on how litigation can go beyond resolving individual cases and contribute to broader changes in law, policy, institutional practice and rights protection . Participants will learn from experienced academics, practitioners and litigators while working with peers from across EU Member States. The programme also includes legal clinics and mentorship to help participants apply what they learn to real-world cases. What the STARLIGHT 2.0 Programme Offers The programme combines several forms of professional learning and collaboration. Practical Legal and Skills Training Participants will take part in in-person training sessions designed to strengthen both their legal knowledge and practical professional skills. The programme s 2026–2027 cohort includes: In-person Charter training Skills training Online legal clinics Mentorship Peer learning Networking with other legal professionals The in-person Charter training is scheduled for 9–11 November 2026 , while the skills training is scheduled for 1–3 March 2027 . Expert Guidance Participants will learn from experienced academics, legal practitioners and strategic litigators with expertise in using the EU Charter and pursuing rights-based litigation. The programme is designed to connect participants with people who have practical experience in developing litigation strategies and using legal cases to achieve systemic change. Legal Clinics and Mentorship Participants will have opportunities to work through real-life cases and develop legal strategies with support from experts and mentors. The legal clinics are an important part of the programme because they allow participants to apply knowledge from the training to practical litigation challenges. European Network STARLIGHT 2.0 also provides participants with an opportunity to connect with legal professionals from across Europe. The programme aims to build a growing community of practitioners who can share knowledge, strategies and best practices while working to strengthen fundamental rights protection. The first cohort included lawyers from NGOs, National Human Rights Institutions and law firms across the EU. Two Thematic Streams Applicants can participate in one of two thematic areas. Democracy and Rule of Law This stream focuses on strategic litigation related to: Democracy Rule of law Fundamental rights Civic space Democratic institutions Systemic rights violations Participants explore how strategic litigation can influence law, policy and public debate. Asylum and Migration The second stream focuses on legal issues involving: Asylum Migration Fundamental rights Protection of migrants and refugees Strategic litigation Applicants should select the stream that most closely aligns with their professional interests and experience. Who Can Apply? The STARLIGHT 2.0 call is open to legal practitioners working in EU Member States . Eligible applicants include legal professionals working in: Law firms Civil society organisations Legal clinics National Human Rights Institutions Applicants should have at least two years of relevant professional experience . The programme is intended for experienced legal professionals who are interested in using strategic litigation to strengthen democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. Eligibility Requirements Applicants should meet the following requirements: Be a legal practitioner working in an EU Member State . Work in a law firm, civil society organisation, legal clinic or National Human Rights Institution. Have at least two years of relevant professional experience . Have an interest in strategic litigation and fundamental rights. Be interested in using the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights in practical litigation. Be prepared to actively participate throughout the programme. The available information does not indicate that the programme is limited to lawyers working in a particular academic specialisation. Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their current legal work connects to the programme s thematic areas. Scholarships and Financial Support Selected participants will receive scholarships covering the training fees and accommodation in Berlin for the three-day in-person legal and skills workshops. However, travel costs are self-funded . This means participants will need to arrange and finance their own travel to and from Berlin, while the programme covers the specified training fees and accommodation. Programme Timeline The current STARLIGHT 2.0 cohort will run from: October 2026 to July 2027 Key in-person training dates include: Charter Training: 9–11 November 2026 Skills Training: 1–3 March 2027 The programme also includes online clinics, mentorship and additional engagement during the programme period. Why Strategic Litigation Matters Strategic litigation can be used to pursue changes that extend beyond the outcome of an individual legal case. A carefully selected case can potentially influence: Legal interpretation Government policy Institutional practice Protection of fundamental rights Public debate Implementation of court decisions STARLIGHT 2.0 is designed to help legal professionals understand how to identify cases with broader potential and develop litigation strategies that can contribute to systemic change. ( DevelopmentAid ) What Participants Can Gain Through the programme, participants can develop: Stronger Knowledge of the EU Charter Gain a deeper understanding of how the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights can be used in strategic litigation. Practical Litigation Skills Learn approaches for developing and pursuing cases with potential for broader impact. Expert Mentorship Receive guidance from experienced legal practitioners and academics. Case-Based Learning Apply programme knowledge to real-life cases through legal clinics. Professional Network Connect with other legal professionals working on fundamental rights and strategic litigation across Europe. Skills for Systemic Impact Learn how litigation can contribute to changes beyond individual cases, including changes to law, policy and public debate. Who Is This Opportunity Best Suited For? STARLIGHT 2.0 may be particularly relevant to legal professionals working on: Human rights Fundamental rights Democracy Rule of law Civic space Asylum Migration Strategic litigation Legal advocacy Rights protection It is especially relevant to practitioners who want to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter as part of their litigation strategy. Application Deadline The application deadline for the current cohort is: 20 September 2026 Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and carefully review all programme requirements before applying. How to Apply Interested legal professionals should apply through the official STARLIGHT 2.0 application process. The programme information and application details are available through the official programme organisers. Programme information: Democracy Reporting International — STARLIGHT 2.0 Applicants should review the official call carefully before submitting their application. Application Tips 1. Demonstrate Your Relevant Experience Clearly explain your legal experience and show how it relates to strategic litigation, fundamental rights, democracy, rule of law, asylum or migration. 2. Explain Your Motivation Be specific about why you want to participate and how the programme will strengthen your professional work. 3. Choose the Appropriate Stream Consider whether your experience and interests are more closely aligned with Democracy Rule of Law or Asylum Migration . 4. Highlight Your Litigation Work Where applicable, describe relevant cases, legal research, advocacy or litigation experience that demonstrates your interest in systemic rights protection. 5. Consider Your Travel Arrangements Although training fees and accommodation in Berlin are covered through scholarships, travel is self-funded . Applicants should plan accordingly. Conclusion STARLIGHT 2.0 – Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe provides legal professionals across EU Member States with an opportunity to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights as a tool for strategic litigation and systemic rights protection. The programme combines legal training, practical skills development, online legal clinics, mentorship and professional networking. Participants can choose between the Democracy Rule of Law and Asylum Migration streams while working with experienced practitioners and peers from across Europe. Selected participants receive scholarships covering training fees and accommodation in Berlin , although travel costs remain the responsibility of participants. Legal practitioners with at least two years of relevant experience who are working in law firms, civil society organisations, legal clinics or National Human Rights Institutions in EU Member States are encouraged to consider applying before the 20 September 2026 deadline . title: CPJ Recruitment 2026: Apply for Remote Press Freedom Positions in Europe and Central Asia
summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists is accepting applications for two remote positions within its Europe and Central Asia programme. These opportunities are intended for experienced professionals with backgrounds in journalism, media freedom, human rights, research, advocacy, humanitarian assistance and regional policy. As verified on September 1, 2026, the official CPJ employment page lists the following vacancies: Program Coordinator, Eastern Europe/Central Asia Researcher, Western and Northern Europe Both positions are classified as remote, Europe-based roles and will be filled through an Employer of Record arrangement. Candidates must be based in the relevant Europe and Central Asia region and possess independent authorization to work from their proposed location. The closing date for both positions is September 10, 2026. CPJ has not specified a precise closing time or time zone, so interested candidates should apply well before the deadline. Overview of the Available CPJ Positions Position Programme Work Arrangement Experience UK Salary Reference Deadline Program Coordinator, Eastern Europe/Central Asia Europe and Central Asia Fully remote, Europe-based At least seven years £72,250–£84,000 September 10, 2026 Researcher, Western and Northern Europe Europe and Central Asia Fully remote, Europe-based At least five years £45,700–£51,500 September 10, 2026 The salary figures above apply as reference ranges for candidates hired in the United Kingdom. Compensation for candidates working from other eligible locations will be determined according to their experience, skills, local market conditions and cost of living. About the Committee to Protect Journalists Founded in 1981, the Committee to Protect Journalists, commonly known as CPJ, is an independent nonprofit organisation that works to defend journalists and advance press freedom around the world. CPJ monitors, verifies and reports attacks against journalists and media workers. Its work includes documenting press freedom violations, advocating for imprisoned or threatened journalists, supporting journalists facing emergencies and encouraging legal and policy reforms that protect freedom of expression. Over more than four decades, CPJ has contributed to efforts that have: Secured the early release of imprisoned journalists. Helped advance accountability for the murders of journalists. Supported legal reforms in countries where freedom of expression has deteriorated. Raised international awareness of attacks on journalists. Produced widely cited research, databases and reports concerning press freedom. Provided assistance to journalists facing physical, digital, legal and psychological threats. Although CPJ is headquartered in New York City, its staff members and contributors work across different regions. The organisation seeks employees who can collaborate effectively across countries, cultures and time zones. Position One: Program Coordinator, Eastern Europe/Central Asia Position Overview The Program Coordinator will lead CPJ’s research, documentation, advocacy and journalist-support activities relating to Eastern Europe and Central Asia. The position sits within CPJ’s Europe and Central Asia programme and reports to the Regional Director for Europe and Central Asia. It is classified within CPJ’s Management II job band. CPJ is looking for an experienced professional with extensive knowledge of press freedom conditions in Russia and Eastern Europe and a strong understanding of the wider regional political, human rights and media environment. The selected candidate will coordinate regional contributors, oversee press freedom monitoring, support journalists facing danger and represent CPJ before media organisations, government representatives, civil society partners and other stakeholders. This is a leadership position requiring both strategic oversight and hands-on involvement in research, reporting, advocacy, crisis response and team management. Team Coordination and Leadership Responsibilities The Program Coordinator will provide day-to-day leadership and supervision to staff members and regional contributors. Responsibilities will include: Establishing clear expectations for staff and contributors. Assigning and delegating work according to programme priorities. Monitoring the quality, accuracy and timeliness of regional work. Coaching and developing team members. Addressing performance or conduct concerns when necessary. Promoting an inclusive, accountable and high-performing team culture. Supporting the recruitment and onboarding of employees and contributors. Managing researchers, correspondents, contractors and other regional contributors. Ensuring that regional work aligns with CPJ’s organisational strategy and standards. Deputising for senior regional leadership when required. Supporting the implementation of wider regional strategies and priorities. Providing crisis-management leadership during urgent or high-risk press freedom situations. Applicants should demonstrate experience supervising people, coordinating distributed teams and maintaining professional standards under pressure. Press Freedom Monitoring, Research and Data Responsibilities A major part of the position involves ensuring that CPJ receives reliable, current and well-documented information concerning attacks on journalists. The Program Coordinator will be expected to: Monitor press freedom developments across Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Document and report attacks, threats and restrictions affecting journalists. Maintain oversight of press freedom case-tracking and advocacy pipelines. Ensure that CPJ’s records concerning imprisoned, missing, killed or targeted journalists remain accurate and current. Identify emerging threats and trends affecting journalists and media organisations. Propose, commission, supervise and conduct regional research. Produce daily reporting, longer analytical reports and multimedia content. Prepare timely news alerts, statements, videos and expert analysis. Develop factual social media material in coordination with CPJ’s communications and social media teams. Contribute to annual regional assessments, planning documents and strategic reviews. The successful candidate must be capable of moving between immediate breaking-news responses and deeper, long-term research projects. Advocacy Responsibilities The Program Coordinator will play a leading role in developing and implementing advocacy strategies intended to improve protections for journalists. Duties will include: Designing regional and country-level press freedom advocacy strategies. Advocating for the release of journalists who have been imprisoned because of their work. Supporting efforts to end impunity in cases involving the killing of journalists. Producing advocacy briefings and other supporting materials. Overseeing the preparation of advocacy content. Developing new projects in response to emerging political and media developments. Presenting CPJ’s research to media outlets, policymakers and other stakeholders. Using evidence and documented cases to influence public and policy discussions. Applicants should understand how research, public communication, stakeholder engagement and policy advocacy can be combined to produce practical pressure for change. Representation and External Engagement The position requires the selected candidate to represent CPJ publicly and maintain a strong network of regional contacts. The Program Coordinator will: Act as a CPJ spokesperson when required. Engage with media outlets, governments, civil society groups and partner organisations. Develop and maintain relationships with policymakers and journalists. Strengthen CPJ’s network of regional media contacts. Establish relationships with human rights defenders and other relevant stakeholders. Develop collaborations, joint initiatives and coalition-based activities. Represent CPJ at national and regional meetings, forums and events. Travel within the region when required. Strong professional judgment will be essential because the position may involve communication about politically sensitive cases and engagement with journalists experiencing serious threats. Journalist Assistance and Safety Responsibilities The Program Coordinator will also support journalists who are experiencing threats, trauma or emergency situations. Responsibilities include: Developing journalist-assistance and advocacy plans. Reviewing requests for assistance from journalists. Assessing urgent cases and identifying appropriate responses. Providing first-responder support and feedback. Coordinating assistance with CPJ’s Journalist Assistance team. Preparing case-related documentation and reports. Working with the Emergencies team to monitor dangerous situations. Responding to new threats affecting journalists. Supporting the delivery of timely and appropriate assistance. Experience supporting people affected by trauma, persecution or emergency conditions is particularly valuable for this role. Internal Coordination and Reporting The Program Coordinator will work with CPJ teams responsible for advocacy, research and journalist assistance to ensure that regional activities contribute to the organisation’s wider objectives. The selected candidate will prepare activity reports, assessments and internal updates and may be assigned other responsibilities consistent with CPJ’s research and advocacy mandate. Required Qualifications for the Program Coordinator Applicants must possess the following qualifications and competencies: A bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience. At least seven years of experience in media or advocacy work connected to regional press freedom issues. Extensive knowledge of Russia, Eastern Europe and the wider Europe and Central Asia region. A deep understanding of the regional geopolitical environment. Demonstrated ability to analyse political, policy and freedom-of-expression issues. The ability to connect political developments with their consequences for journalists and press freedom. Strong research, analysis and reporting skills. Experience writing concise and high-quality reports. The ability to interpret, assess and accurately summarise reports and data. Fluency in spoken and written English. Fluency in spoken and written Russian. Working proficiency in other relevant regional languages. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong interpersonal, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills. Excellent organisational abilities and close attention to detail. Strong time-management skills and a record of meeting deadlines. Effective analytical and problem-solving abilities. The capacity to work with integrity, professionalism and confidentiality. Experience leading teams and working with senior managers. Willingness and ability to travel occasionally within the region. Proficiency in Google Workspace applications. Because the role includes emergency response and politically sensitive work, candidates must be able to make careful decisions, protect confidential information and remain effective in high-pressure situations. Preferred Qualifications for the Program Coordinator CPJ considers the following qualifications desirable: Knowledge of additional regional languages. An established network of professional contacts across the region. Expertise concerning online or digital harms, including surveillance. Experience contributing to policy development. Multimedia or data-journalism experience. Experience supporting journalists or other individuals affected by trauma. Experience managing journalist-assistance cases. Applicants who meet all essential requirements should not necessarily exclude themselves merely because they do not possess every preferred qualification. Work Location and Schedule The Program Coordinator position is: Fully remote. Located in Europe. Intended for a candidate based in the Europe and Central Asia region. Filled through an Employer of Record. Subject to occasional regional travel. Required to attend meetings conducted on United States Eastern Time when necessary. Remote status does not mean that applications are automatically accepted from every country. The application form expressly asks applicants to state where they are currently based, where they intend to work and whether they possess independent work authorization in that location. The vacancy does not state that CPJ will sponsor a visa, work permit or relocation. Program Coordinator Salary Compensation will depend on the selected candidate’s: Professional experience. Relevant skills. Country of employment. Local labour-market conditions. Cost of living. For a candidate hired in the United Kingdom, CPJ provides an expected annual salary reference of: £72,250 to £84,000 Candidates based in another eligible country should not assume that the UK salary range will apply. CPJ will determine location-specific compensation under the applicable Employer of Record arrangement. Position Two: Researcher, Western and Northern Europe Position Overview CPJ is also recruiting a Researcher focusing on Western and Northern Europe. The position is part of the Europe and Central Asia programme and reports to the Program Coordinator for Europe and Central Asia. The position is classified within the Researchers and Associates I job band and identified as a mid-level role. The Researcher will monitor, investigate, verify and document attacks on the press and other developments affecting media freedom. The position also involves preparing research and advocacy materials, supporting regional strategy, representing CPJ when required and assisting journalists facing threats or emergencies. The successful candidate must have substantial knowledge of media, press freedom and human rights issues in Europe and Central Asia, with particular strength in Western and Northern Europe. Monitoring, Data Collection and Documentation Responsibilities The Researcher will be responsible for tracking press freedom developments and ensuring that CPJ’s reporting is supported by verified evidence. Responsibilities include: Monitoring press freedom developments across Europe and Central Asia. Focusing particularly on Western and Northern Europe. Investigating and documenting arrests of journalists. Monitoring censorship and restrictions on media organisations. Recording physical attacks and threats against journalists. Examining legal harassment directed at journalists and media outlets. Monitoring transnational repression affecting journalists. Documenting other threats to press freedom. Maintaining current information in CPJ’s databases. Updating records concerning imprisoned, missing, killed or targeted journalists. Monitoring breaking news and emerging developments. Alerting the Program Coordinator promptly when an urgent issue arises. Developing and maintaining databases of media, government and civil-society contacts. Candidates must be able to verify information carefully and distinguish credible evidence from incomplete, misleading or politically motivated claims. Research and Writing Responsibilities The Researcher will produce content for CPJ’s reporting, advocacy and public communications. The selected candidate will: Initiate and write reports concerning regional press freedom. Produce advocacy documents and background materials. Write timely news alerts and public statements. Prepare expert analysis concerning regional developments. Conduct original research on press freedom issues. Prepare research notes in accordance with CPJ standards. Write factual and engaging social media content. Coordinate public-facing material with CPJ’s social media team. Contribute to longer-term research and reporting initiatives. Excellent English writing and reporting skills are essential. Applicants must be able to produce accurate material quickly without sacrificing verification or journalistic standards. Advocacy Responsibilities The Researcher will support and participate in CPJ’s regional advocacy activities. Responsibilities will include: Representing CPJ at relevant conferences and meetings. Participating in meetings with government authorities. Engaging with journalists, partner organisations and policymakers. Helping develop advocacy strategies for Europe and Central Asia. Implementing advocacy activities in coordination with the Program Coordinator and Regional Director. Participating in online and in-person meetings that advance CPJ’s press freedom objectives. The role requires candidates who can explain complex political and media issues clearly to different audiences. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination The Researcher will build relationships with people and organisations relevant to CPJ’s work. This includes: Developing relationships with journalists. Maintaining contacts with human rights organisations. Engaging with civil society and other regional stakeholders. Coordinating joint activities that advance CPJ’s objectives. Collaborating with CPJ’s advocacy, research and assistance teams. Presenting CPJ research to media outlets and other stakeholders. Helping influence coverage of important press freedom developments. A strong regional network is preferred, although it is not listed as an absolute requirement. Journalist Assistance Responsibilities The Researcher will support CPJ’s work with journalists who require assistance. Duties include: Researching and verifying journalist-assistance requests. Preparing assistance documentation in accordance with CPJ’s internal framework. Coordinating with the Emergencies team. Communicating and coordinating with journalists receiving support. Helping ensure that assistance decisions are based on accurate and properly documented information. Experience with trauma-related cases or journalist-assistance work is considered an advantage. Translation and Additional Support The Researcher may be asked to translate interviews, documents and other materials between English and relevant regional languages. The selected candidate may also perform other responsibilities that fall within CPJ’s research and advocacy mandate. Required Qualifications for the Researcher Applicants must possess: At least five years of experience researching, reporting and publishing on global human rights and political issues; or equivalent experience in advocacy and humanitarian assistance. Strong knowledge of Europe and Central Asia. A solid understanding of regional media and human rights issues. Excellent English writing and reporting skills. Proficiency in at least one additional language relevant to the position. Strong interpersonal and organisational skills. Effective time-management abilities. The ability to work independently and collaboratively. The ability to perform effectively in a fast-paced working environment. A clear commitment to press freedom. The capacity to work with minimal supervision. Unlike the Program Coordinator vacancy, the Researcher listing does not prescribe a bachelor’s degree as a mandatory qualification. Relevant professional experience, subject knowledge and language ability are central requirements. Preferred Qualifications for the Researcher The following experience and capabilities are desirable: Knowledge of additional regional languages. Strong professional networks within the region. Expertise relating to digital or online harms. Policy-development experience. Multimedia journalism experience. Data-journalism skills. Experience supporting trauma-related cases. Previous involvement in journalist-assistance work. Researcher Work Location and Schedule The Researcher position is: Fully remote. Located in Europe. Intended for a candidate based in the Europe or Central Asia region. Filled through an Employer of Record. Required to attend meetings conducted on United States Eastern Time when necessary. Applicants must possess independent authorization to work in the city and country from which they intend to perform the role. The announcement does not promise work-visa sponsorship or relocation assistance. Researcher Salary Compensation will depend on experience, skills and location. For candidates hired in the United Kingdom, the expected annual salary range is: £45,700 to £51,500 Candidates hired in other eligible locations may receive a different salary based on local market conditions and cost-of-living differences. title: UN Junior Professional Officer Programme 2026 | Three Positions Open
summary: The United Nations Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme 2026 is inviting applications from qualified young professionals for three JPO positions within the United Nations system. The current call features opportunities in Political Affairs in New York, Humanitarian Affairs in East Jerusalem, and UN System Coordination in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire . All three positions are funded by Belgium and have an initial one-year contract that may be renewed annually for a maximum period of three years. ( FPS Foreign Affairs ) The application deadline for all three positions is 18 September 2026 at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (New York) . ( FPS Foreign Affairs ) About the UN Junior Professional Officer Programme The Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme is a United Nations training initiative that provides young professionals with an opportunity to gain practical experience within UN organisations, funds, programmes, and offices involved in development and international cooperation. Through the programme, JPOs work within UN organisations connected to Belgium s international development cooperation policy. Depending on the position, assignments can be based in partner countries, regional offices, or headquarters. JPOs receive professional training and guidance from senior staff members and can become involved in areas including: Programme design Programme formulation Programme implementation Programme monitoring Programme evaluation Policy and coordination work Development and humanitarian activities The Belgian government currently funds JPO positions across 18 UN organisations, funds, programmes and offices , including UNDP, UNICEF, WFP, FAO, UNHCR, WHO, UNFPA, UN Women, UNEP, IOM, OHCHR and OCHA. Current JPO Opportunities Three positions are currently available under the 2026 Belgian JPO call. 1. JPO in Political Affairs – Support to UN Reform Organisation: United Nations Executive Office of the Secretary-General (EOSG), Office of the Under-Secretary-General for Policy, UN80 Secretariat Location: New York, USA Field: Political Affairs / UN Reform The position focuses on supporting work related to UN reform and political affairs within the UN80 Secretariat. Eligibility and Qualifications Applicants must: Hold Belgian citizenship . Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026. Be born on or after 1 January 1994 . Hold an advanced university degree, such as a master s degree or equivalent , in: Political Science International Relations International Humanitarian Law Human Rights Social Sciences or another related field. Have at least two years of relevant professional experience in political affairs, development and/or humanitarian work. Have relevant experience with governments, international organisations, NGOs or research institutes. Experience with the UN or other international or non-governmental organisations is considered an advantage. Strong research, analytical and writing skills, as well as organisational abilities, are also preferred. Language Requirements Fluent English is required. Knowledge of French is desirable, while knowledge of another official UN language is an advantage. Important Experience Requirement Applicants work experience within the UN organisation to which they are applying must not exceed one year , including internships, UN Volunteers and consultancies. Relevant internships and volunteering may be counted at 50%. 2. JPO in Humanitarian Affairs Organisation: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Operations and Advocacy Division, Country Office in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) Location: East Jerusalem Field: Humanitarian Affairs This position is focused on humanitarian affairs and supports work related to humanitarian operations and advocacy. Eligibility and Qualifications Applicants must: Hold Belgian citizenship . Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026. Be born on or after 1 January 1994 . Hold an advanced university degree, such as a Master s degree , in: Political or Social Science International Relations Public Administration Law Economics Engineering Earth Sciences A related field. Have at least two years of relevant professional experience in humanitarian affairs, emergency preparedness, crisis or emergency relief management, rehabilitation, development, or related areas. Have experience in information analysis . Experience working with international humanitarian agencies, the UN system, or in the occupied Palestinian territory context is considered desirable. Language Requirements Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Arabic is an advantage. As with the other positions, work experience within the UN organisation to which the candidate is applying must not exceed one year, including internships, UNV and consultancies. 3. JPO in Coordination – UN System Coordination Organisation: United Nations Resident Coordinator System (RCS), Resident Coordinator Office (RCO) Location: Abidjan, Côte d Ivoire Field: UN System Coordination This position focuses on coordination within the UN Resident Coordinator System and provides an opportunity to contribute to cooperation and coordination across the UN system. Eligibility and Qualifications Applicants must: Hold Belgian citizenship . Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026. Be born on or after 1 January 1994 . Hold a Master s degree or equivalent advanced degree in: Development International Relations Political Science Economics Management A related field. Have at least two years of professional experience in a relevant field . Language Requirements Fluency in French is required. Knowledge of other official UN languages, particularly English, is an advantage. General Eligibility Requirements Although the three positions have different academic and professional requirements, the current Belgian-funded JPO call has several common eligibility conditions. Belgian Citizenship The current vacancies explicitly state that candidates must hold Belgian citizenship . The Belgian Foreign Affairs website explains that most Belgian-funded JPO positions are reserved for Belgian nationals. A limited number of positions may be reserved for candidates from Belgium s partner countries, but this must be specifically indicated in the relevant vacancy announcement. ( FPS Foreign Affairs ) Therefore, applicants should not assume that every Belgian-funded JPO position is open to applicants from all countries. Age Requirement Candidates must be 32 years old or younger on 31 December 2026 . For the current positions, this means candidates must have been born on or after 1 January 1994 . Master s Degree A master s degree or equivalent advanced university degree is required, although the acceptable field differs according to the position. Professional Experience The current positions generally require a minimum of two years of relevant professional experience . Applicants should make sure that their experience is directly related to the responsibilities and subject area of the position for which they are applying. UN Experience Limitation For the current positions, professional experience within the specific UN organisation to which the applicant is applying should not exceed one year , including internships, UN Volunteers and consultancies. Relevant internships and volunteering may be counted at 50%. How the JPO Programme Works JPOs work within participating UN organisations and receive professional training from experienced senior staff. They may contribute to different stages of programme and policy work, including: Defining programmes. Formulating programmes. Implementing programmes. Monitoring programmes. Evaluating programmes. This allows young professionals to gain experience within the UN system while developing practical knowledge in international development, humanitarian affairs, policy, coordination and related fields. Contract Duration The initial JPO appointment is for one year . Subject to a positive performance evaluation, the appointment may be renewed annually, up to a maximum total period of three years . Salary and Employment Conditions JPOs receive the international status of the UN organisation that recruits them. Their salary is paid in US dollars and is based on the United Nations salary scales. Belgium also contributes toward the pension component through the Belgian National Social Security Office or the United Nations pension fund, as applicable. At the end of the JPO contract, there are no special placement facilities provided by Belgium s Directorate-General for Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid. However, the experience and knowledge gained through the programme can improve participants prospects for progressing within international organisations. Application Process Applications must be submitted directly to the relevant UN organisation through the application system indicated in the vacancy announcement. Candidates should consult the full job description before applying because the current Belgian Foreign Affairs page only displays the vacancy information during the application period. The current vacancies direct applicants to the UNDESA recruitment website and its eRecruitment system. Application portal: UNDESA JPO Application Portal Applicants should select the appropriate position and follow the instructions provided by the UN recruitment system. Application Documents and Selection The Belgian Foreign Affairs guidance explains that shortlisted candidates may be required to provide copies of their: University degree(s) Employment certificates Identity card or passport The initial preselection is based on the candidate s Personal History/CV and Cover Letter . Shortlisted candidates are interviewed online. Tips for Preparing Your Application The Belgian Foreign Affairs department provides several recommendations for applicants. Read the Vacancy Carefully Study the required qualifications and responsibilities before completing the application. Use Relevant Keywords The department recommends using keywords appearing in the vacancy and making them clearly visible in the application. Be Specific Avoid vague descriptions of your experience. Instead, provide concrete examples of relevant work and the results you achieved. Provide Accurate Dates When completing your application, provide accurate information, including the month and year where requested. Avoid Unnecessary Acronyms Write out abbreviations and acronyms rather than assuming that the selection panel will understand them. Make Your Motivation Precise Because the JPO selection process is described as highly competitive, applicants should ensure that their motivation clearly demonstrates why their background matches the specific position. Application Deadline The deadline for all three current Belgian-funded JPO positions is: 18 September 2026 at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (New York). Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. Applicants will receive confirmation that their application has been received, and only shortlisted candidates will subsequently be contacted. Current Positions at a Glance Position Organisation Location Key Field Deadline JPO in Political Affairs – Support to UN Reform UN Executive Office of the Secretary-General New York, USA Political Affairs / UN Reform 18 Sept. 2026 JPO in Humanitarian Affairs OCHA East Jerusalem Humanitarian Affairs 18 Sept. 2026 JPO in Coordination – UN System Coordination UN Resident Coordinator System Abidjan, Côte d Ivoire UN Coordination 18 Sept. 2026 The positions all have an initial one-year duration, renewable annually up to three years. Who Can Apply? Category of people who qualify: Young professionals who hold Belgian citizenship, are no older than 32 at the end of 2026, possess a relevant master s degree or equivalent advanced degree, and have at least two years of relevant professional experience. The precise academic background, work experience and language requirements depend on the JPO position selected. Eligible nationality: The three current vacancies are specifically for Belgian citizens . Conclusion The UN Junior Professional Officer Programme 2026 provides an opportunity for qualified young Belgian professionals to gain practical experience within the United Nations system. The current call offers three positions spanning political affairs and UN reform, humanitarian affairs, and UN system coordination , with placements in New York, East Jerusalem, and Abidjan . The programme provides structured professional experience, exposure to international organisations, senior-level mentorship, and the opportunity to contribute to UN programmes and policy work. Successful JPO appointments begin with one year and can potentially be extended to a maximum of three years following positive evaluations. Eligible candidates should carefully match their academic qualifications and professional experience to the specific vacancy and submit their application before 18 September 2026 at 6:00 PM Eastern Time .
